title.en: The First World War, and votes for women
title.fr: La Première Guerre mondiale et le droit de vote des femmes

text.en: More than 7,000 Canadians signed up to fight in the South African War of 1899–1902, which most people call the Boer War. Over 260 of them died.
text.fr: Plus de 7 000 Canadiens se sont portés volontaires pour combattre pendant la guerre d'Afrique du Sud de 1899-1902, que la plupart des gens appellent la guerre des Boers. Plus de 260 d'entre eux sont morts.

source.quote: Over 7,000 volunteered to fight in the South African War (1899–1902), popularly known as the Boer War, and over 260 died.

text.en: Canada had only eight million people, yet more than 600,000 Canadians served in the First World War. Most of them were volunteers.
text.fr: Le Canada ne comptait que huit millions d'habitants, et pourtant plus de 600 000 Canadiens ont servi pendant la Première Guerre mondiale. La plupart étaient des volontaires.

source.quote: More than 600,000 Canadians served in the war, most of them volunteers, out of a total population of eight million.

text.en: In April 1917, the Canadian Corps took Vimy Ridge. 10,000 Canadians were killed or wounded there.
text.fr: En avril 1917, le Corps canadien s'est emparé de la crête de Vimy. 10 000 Canadiens y ont été tués ou blessés.

source.quote: The Canadian Corps captured Vimy Ridge in April 1917, with 10,000 killed or wounded

text.en: Ottawa held more than 8,000 people who had been subjects of Austria-Hungary, mostly Ukrainian men, as “enemy aliens.” They were kept in 24 labour camps across Canada.
text.fr: Ottawa a détenu plus de 8 000 personnes qui avaient été sujets de l'Autriche-Hongrie, surtout des hommes ukrainiens, comme « étrangers ennemis ». Elles ont été gardées dans 24 camps de travail partout au Canada.

source.quote: Ottawa interned over 8,000 former Austro-Hungarian subjects, mainly Ukrainian men, as “enemy aliens” in 24 labour camps across Canada

text.en: In the last hundred days of the war, the Canadian Corps was led by General Sir Arthur Currie. Discover Canada calls him Canada's greatest soldier.
text.fr: Pendant les cent derniers jours de la guerre, le Corps canadien était commandé par le général sir Arthur Currie. Découvrir le Canada le décrit comme le plus grand soldat du Canada.

source.quote: under the command of General Sir Arthur Currie, Canada’s greatest soldier

text.en: The First World War ended with the Armistice on November 11, 1918.
text.fr: La Première Guerre mondiale a pris fin avec l'armistice du 11 novembre 1918.

source.quote: the war ended in the Armistice on November 11, 1918.

text.en: When Confederation came, only white men who were adults and owned property could vote.
text.fr: Au moment de la Confédération, seuls les hommes blancs adultes qui possédaient une propriété pouvaient voter.

source.quote: the vote was limited to property-owning adult white males.

text.en: Dr. Emily Stowe founded the movement for women's right to vote in Canada. She was also the first Canadian woman to work as a doctor in Canada.
text.fr: La Dre Emily Stowe a fondé au Canada le mouvement pour le droit de vote des femmes. Elle a aussi été la première Canadienne à pratiquer la médecine au Canada.

source.quote: Its founder in Canada was Dr. Emily Stowe, the first Canadian woman to practise medicine in Canada.

text.en: In 1916, Manitoba was the first province to give women the right to vote.
text.fr: En 1916, le Manitoba a été la première province à accorder le droit de vote aux femmes.

source.quote: In 1916, Manitoba became the first province to grant voting rights to women.

text.en: In 1918, most women who were Canadian citizens and 21 or older got the right to vote in federal elections.
text.fr: En 1918, la plupart des femmes qui étaient citoyennes canadiennes et âgées de 21 ans ou plus ont obtenu le droit de vote aux élections fédérales.

source.quote: In 1918, most Canadian female citizens aged 21 and over were granted the right to vote in federal elections.

text.en: Agnes Macphail was a farmer and a teacher. In 1921 she became the first woman elected as an MP.
text.fr: Agnes Macphail était agricultrice et enseignante. En 1921, elle est devenue la première femme élue députée.

source.quote: In 1921 Agnes Macphail, a farmer and teacher, became the first woman MP.

text.en: Thanks to the work of Thérèse Casgrain and others, women in Quebec got the vote in 1940.
text.fr: Grâce au travail de Thérèse Casgrain et d'autres personnes, les femmes du Québec ont obtenu le droit de vote en 1940.

source.quote: Due to the work of Thérèse Casgrain and others, Quebec granted women the vote in 1940.

text.en: On Remembrance Day, Canadians wear a red poppy. At 11 o'clock on the 11th day of the 11th month, they stop for a moment of silence.
text.fr: Le jour du Souvenir, les Canadiens portent un coquelicot rouge. À 11 heures, le 11e jour du 11e mois, ils observent un moment de silence.

source.quote: Canadians wear the red poppy and observe a moment of silence at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month

text.en: Lieutenant Colonel John McCrae, a Canadian army doctor, wrote the poem “In Flanders Fields” in 1915.
text.fr: Le lieutenant-colonel John McCrae, un médecin militaire canadien, a écrit le poème « Au champ d'honneur » (In Flanders Fields) en 1915.

source.quote: Canadian medical officer Lieutenant Colonel John McCrae composed the poem “In Flanders Fields” in 1915
